aloysius_gonzaga_religious.bio: Born heir to a noble Italian house, he gave up his title to join the Jesuits. He died at twenty-three after nursing victims of plague in Rome, and is patron of young people.

andrew_dung_lac_priest_and_companions_ma.bio: A Vietnamese priest who gave his life with 116 companions—priests, catechists and lay people—during waves of persecution in Vietnam. They were canonized together in 1988.

apollinaris_of_ravenna_bishop.bio: Remembered as the first bishop of Ravenna, he preached through repeated imprisonment and exile. The great basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe bears his name.

ascension_of_the_lord.bio: Forty days after Easter, the risen Christ was taken up into heaven before the eyes of his apostles, promising to send the Holy Spirit and to come again.

athanasius_of_alexandria_bishop.bio: Bishop of Alexandria who defended the divinity of Christ against the Arian heresy. Exiled five times, he never gave way, and is honored as a Doctor of the Church.

augustine_of_hippo_bishop.bio: After a restless youth he was converted in Milan, moved by the prayers of his mother, Monica. As bishop of Hippo he wrote the Confessions and The City of God; he is a Doctor of the Church.

baptism_of_the_lord.bio: Jesus is baptized by John in the Jordan. The heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice declares, 'This is my beloved Son.'

bartholomew_apostle.bio: One of the Twelve, often identified with Nathanael, of whom Jesus said, 'Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no guile.' Tradition says he preached in the East and was martyred there.

bernardine_of_siena_priest.bio: A Franciscan preacher who walked the length of Italy calling people to conversion. He spread devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus, often showing the letters IHS on a tablet.

cajetan_of_thiene_priest.bio: A priest of Vicenza who co-founded the Theatines to renew the clergy. He opened hospitals and pawnshops for the poor, and is patron of job-seekers.

camillus_de_lellis_priest.bio: A soldier and gambler converted after years of wandering, he founded the Camillians to serve the sick, wearing a red cross. He is patron of nurses, doctors and hospitals.

casimir_of_poland.bio: A Polish prince known for his prayer, purity and generosity to the poor. He died young of tuberculosis and is patron of Poland and Lithuania.

catherine_of_siena_virgin.bio: A Dominican laywoman and mystic who cared for the sick and urged the pope to return from Avignon to Rome. She is a Doctor of the Church and patron of Italy and Europe.

cecilia_of_rome_virgin.bio: A Roman martyr who, tradition says, sang to God in her heart on her wedding day. She is patron of musicians and church music.

commemoration_of_all_the_faithful_depart.bio: All Souls' Day. The Church prays for all who have died, that they may be purified and come to rest in the peace of God.

cyril_of_alexandria_bishop.bio: Patriarch of Alexandria who led the Council of Ephesus in 431, defending the title of Mary as Mother of God (Theotokos). He is a Doctor of the Church.

damasus_i_pope.bio: Pope who commissioned St. Jerome to translate the Bible into Latin, the Vulgate. He honored the martyrs by restoring the catacombs and writing verses for their tombs.

easter_sunday.bio: Christ is risen. The empty tomb at dawn is the heart of the Christian faith, and the Easter feast is kept for eight days as a single day of joy.

easter_monday.bio: “Behold, Jesus met them and said, ‘Hail!’ And they came up and took hold of his feet and worshiped him. Then Jesus said to them, ‘Do not be afraid; go and tell my brethren to go to Galilee, and there they will see me.’”

easter_tuesday.bio: “Jesus said to her, ‘Mary.’ She turned and said to him in Hebrew, ‘Rabboni!’ (which means Teacher).”

easter_wednesday.bio: “When he was at table with them, he took the bread and blessed, and broke it, and gave it to them. And their eyes were opened and they recognized him; and he vanished out of their sight.”

easter_friday.bio: “That disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, ‘It is the Lord!’ When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his clothes, for he was stripped for work, and sprang into the sea.”

easter_saturday.bio: “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to the whole creation.”

elizabeth_of_hungary_religious.bio: A Hungarian princess and widow who gave her wealth to the poor and built a hospital at Marburg. She died at twenty-four and is patron of Franciscan tertiaries and charities.

elizabeth_of_portugal.bio: Queen of Portugal, known as a peacemaker within her own family and between kings. After her husband's death she lived as a Poor Clare tertiary.

eusebius_of_vercelli_bishop.bio: First bishop of Vercelli, he lived in community with his clergy and suffered exile for defending the Nicene faith against the Arians.

fabian_i_pope.bio: Chosen pope, the story goes, when a dove settled on his head. He organized the Church of Rome and died a martyr under the emperor Decius.

fidelis_of_sigmaringen_priest.bio: A lawyer who became a Capuchin friar, known as the 'poor man's lawyer'. He was killed while preaching in Switzerland during the wars of religion.

francis_de_sales_bishop.bio: Bishop of Geneva, famed for gentleness and for teaching that holiness is for everyone. His Introduction to the Devout Life is still read; he is patron of writers and journalists.

george_of_lydda_martyr.bio: A soldier martyred under Diocletian, honored in East and West. The legend of his slaying the dragon made him the model of the Christian knight; he is patron of England.

gertrude_the_great_virgin.bio: A Benedictine nun of Helfta whose visions and writings helped spread devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

gregory_i_the_great_pope.bio: A Roman prefect turned monk, then pope. He sent missionaries to England, reformed the liturgy and cared for Rome in famine and plague. He is a Doctor of the Church.

henry_ii_emperor.bio: Holy Roman Emperor who supported church reform and founded the diocese of Bamberg, where he is buried beside his wife, St. Cunigunde.

hildegard_of_bingen_abbess.bio: A Benedictine abbess, visionary, composer and writer on medicine and nature. Declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012.

holy_guardian_angels.bio: The Church gives thanks for the angels God sends to guard and guide each person: 'He will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.'

ignatius_of_antioch_bishop.bio: Bishop of Antioch who was taken to Rome to die in the arena. On the way he wrote seven letters, asking the Christians not to prevent his martyrdom: 'I am the wheat of God.'

ignatius_of_loyola_priest.bio: A Basque soldier converted while recovering from a cannonball wound. He wrote the Spiritual Exercises and founded the Society of Jesus, the Jesuits.

immaculate_conception_of_the_blessed_vir.bio: The Church celebrates that Mary, by a singular grace, was preserved from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception. Patronal feast of the United States.

isidore_of_seville_bishop.bio: Archbishop of Seville whose Etymologies gathered the learning of the ancient world for the Middle Ages. A Doctor of the Church.

isidore_the_farmer.bio: A farm laborer near Madrid, devoted to daily Mass and to the poor. Legend says angels ploughed his fields while he prayed. He is patron of farmers.

james_apostle.bio: Son of Zebedee and brother of John, one of the three closest to Jesus. The first apostle to be martyred, he is venerated at Santiago de Compostela.

jane_frances_de_chantal_religious.bio: A widowed mother of four who, guided by St. Francis de Sales, founded the Order of the Visitation for women who could not bear the rigors of older orders.

januarius_i_of_benevento_bishop.bio: Bishop of Benevento martyred under Diocletian. His blood, kept in a glass vial in Naples, is venerated there; he is the city's patron.

john_apostle.bio: The beloved disciple, who leaned on Jesus at the Last Supper and stood at the foot of the cross. The Gospel, letters and Revelation are attributed to him.

john_chrysostom_bishop.bio: Archbishop of Constantinople whose preaching earned him the name 'Golden Mouth'. He died in exile for denouncing corruption, and is a Doctor of the Church.

john_damascene_priest.bio: A monk near Jerusalem who defended the veneration of holy images during the iconoclast controversy. A Doctor of the Church.

john_de_brebeuf_isaac_jogues_priests_and.bio: French Jesuit missionaries and lay companions who lived among the Huron and Iroquois peoples and were martyred there. They are the patron saints of North America.

john_fisher_bishop_and_thomas_more_marty.bio: A bishop and a Lord Chancellor of England who refused to accept King Henry VIII as head of the Church. More went to his death 'the King's good servant, but God's first.'

john_henry_newman_priest.bio: An Anglican leader of the Oxford Movement who became a Catholic and later a cardinal. A writer of rare clarity, he was canonized in 2019.

john_leonardi_priest.bio: A pharmacist turned priest in Lucca, he founded the Clerks Regular of the Mother of God and helped establish what became the Church's college for the missions.

john_mary_vianney_priest.bio: The Curé of Ars, a village priest who spent up to sixteen hours a day hearing confessions. He is patron of parish priests.

john_of_avila_priest.bio: A Spanish priest and preacher, adviser to saints such as Teresa of Ávila and John of God. Declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012.

john_of_kanty_priest.bio: A professor at the University of Kraków, known for his learning and his great generosity to the poor.

john_of_the_cross_priest.bio: A Carmelite friar who worked with St. Teresa of Ávila to reform the order. His poems, including The Dark Night, are among the treasures of Spanish literature. A Doctor of the Church.

josaphat_kuntsevych_bishop.bio: A Ukrainian Greek Catholic archbishop of Polotsk who worked for unity between Eastern Christians and Rome, and was martyred for it.

joseph_of_calasanz_priest.bio: A Spanish priest who opened one of Europe's first free public schools, in Rome,, and founded the Piarists to teach poor children.

leo_i_the_great_pope.bio: Pope whose letter, the Tome, guided the Council of Chalcedon on the two natures of Christ. He met Attila the Hun and persuaded him to turn back from Rome.

mary_magdalene_de_pazzi_virgin.bio: A Carmelite nun of Florence known for her ecstasies and her prayer for the renewal of the Church.

mary_mother_of_god.bio: On the octave day of Christmas the Church honors Mary under her greatest title, Theotokos, the Mother of God, and begins the new year in her care.

matthias_apostle.bio: Chosen by lot after the Ascension to take the place of Judas among the Twelve. Tradition holds that he preached and died a martyr.

monica_of_hippo.bio: Mother of St. Augustine, who prayed for his conversion for many years. She died at Ostia shortly after his baptism.

nativity_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.bio: The birthday of Mary, daughter of Joachim and Anne, celebrated nine months after the feast of her Immaculate Conception.

nereus_of_terracina_and_achilleus_of_ter.bio: Roman soldiers who, according to an early inscription, laid down their arms on becoming Christians and were martyred.

our_lady_of_loreto.bio: The Holy House of Loreto, venerated as the home of the Holy Family at Nazareth, has drawn pilgrims for centuries. Our Lady of Loreto is patron of aviators.

our_lady_of_lourdes.bio: In 1858 the Virgin Mary appeared eighteen times to Bernadette Soubirous at Lourdes, calling herself 'the Immaculate Conception'. The spring there has drawn countless pilgrims and sick people.

our_lady_of_mount_carmel.bio: Patronal feast of the Carmelites, who take their name from Mount Carmel in the Holy Land. Devotion to the brown scapular is linked to this feast.

our_lady_of_sorrows.bio: Mary's sorrows, from Simeon's prophecy to the burial of her Son. 'A sword will pierce your own soul too.'

our_lady_of_the_rosary.bio: Instituted after the victory at Lepanto in 1571, attributed to the praying of the Rosary. The Rosary is a meditation on the life of Christ with Mary.

paulinus_of_nola_bishop.bio: A wealthy Roman senator and poet who gave away his fortune with his wife, Therasia, and became bishop of Nola.

perpetua_of_carthage_and_felicity_of_car.bio: A young noblewoman and her pregnant slave, martyred together in the arena at Carthage. Perpetua's own prison diary survives.

peter_canisius_priest.bio: A Dutch Jesuit whose catechisms renewed Catholic life in Germany after the Reformation. A Doctor of the Church.

philip_neri_priest.bio: The 'Apostle of Rome', known for his joy and humor. He founded the Oratory, where prayer, music and conversation brought many back to faith.

pius_v_pope.bio: A Dominican pope who carried out the reforms of the Council of Trent, issued the Roman Missal and Catechism, and called Christendom to pray the Rosary before Lepanto.

queenship_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.bio: A week after the Assumption, the Church honors Mary as Queen of heaven and earth, crowned beside her Son.

robert_bellarmine_bishop.bio: A Jesuit cardinal and theologian who wrote catechisms and great works of controversy with humility and charity. A Doctor of the Church.

romuald_of_ravenna_abbot.bio: A nobleman of Ravenna who became a monk and founded the Camaldolese, uniting the hermit's life with community.

rose_of_lima_virgin.bio: The first canonized saint of the Americas, she lived a life of prayer and penance in her family's garden in Lima, serving the poor and sick.

sebastian_of_milan_martyr.bio: A Roman soldier who encouraged Christians in prison. Shot with arrows and left for dead, he survived, confronted the emperor, and was martyred.

seven_holy_founders_of_the_servite_order.bio: Seven merchants of Florence who left their businesses to live together in prayer and penance, founding the Order of Servants of Mary.

sixtus_ii_pope_and_companions_martyrs.bio: Pope Sixtus was seized while celebrating Mass in the catacombs and beheaded with four of his deacons. His deacon Lawrence followed days later.

thomas_aquinas_priest.bio: A Dominican friar and the Church's great theologian. His Summa Theologiae united faith and reason; he is the 'Angelic Doctor' and patron of students.

thomas_becket_bishop.bio: Archbishop of Canterbury and former chancellor to King Henry II, murdered in his cathedral for defending the freedom of the Church.

timothy_of_ephesus_and_titus_of_crete_bi.bio: Companions of St. Paul, who wrote them the 'pastoral letters'. Timothy led the church at Ephesus, Titus the church on Crete.

turibius_of_mogrovejo_bishop.bio: A Spanish lawyer made archbishop of Lima, who travelled thousands of miles across his diocese, learning local languages and defending the native peoples.

wenceslaus_i_of_bohemia_martyr.bio: Duke of Bohemia, the 'Good King Wenceslas' of the carol, known for his piety and charity. He was murdered by his brother and is patron of the Czech lands.

palm_sunday_of_the_passion_of_the_lord.bio: Jesus enters Jerusalem to the cries of 'Hosanna!', the crowds laying palms before him. Holy Week begins.

friday_of_the_passion_of_the_lord.bio: Good Friday. Christ dies on the cross. 'Behold the wood of the Cross, on which hung the salvation of the world.'

holy_saturday.bio: The Lord lies in the tomb. The Church waits in silence until the Easter Vigil, when the new fire is kindled in the dark.

divine_mercy_sunday.bio: The Sunday after Easter, devoted to the mercy of Christ as revealed to St. Faustina Kowalska: 'Jesus, I trust in you.'

day_of_prayer_for_the_legal_protection_o.bio: A day of prayer and penance in the United States for the protection of human life, entrusted to Our Lady of Guadalupe, patroness of the unborn.

albert_the_great_bishop.bio: A German Dominican and bishop who taught St. Thomas Aquinas and wrote on everything from theology to botany. A Doctor of the Church and patron of scientists.

alphonsus_mary_liguori_bishop.bio: A Neapolitan lawyer turned priest who founded the Redemptorists. His writings on prayer and moral theology made him a Doctor of the Church.

blaise_of_sebaste_bishop.bio: A bishop of Armenia who, tradition says, saved a boy choking on a fishbone. The blessing of throats is given on his feast.

boniface_of_mainz_bishop.bio: An English monk who became the apostle of Germany, famously felling the sacred oak of Thor. He was martyred in Frisia.

bridget_of_sweden_religious.bio: A Swedish noblewoman, mother of eight, whose visions and counsel reached popes and kings. She founded the Bridgettines and is a patron of Europe.

columban_of_luxeuil_abbot.bio: An Irish monk who founded monasteries across France and Italy, from Luxeuil to Bobbio, carrying Irish learning to the continent.

elizabeth_ann_seton_religious.bio: A New York widow and convert who founded the Sisters of Charity and opened a free Catholic school at Emmitsburg, a seed of America's parish schools. The first native-born American saint.

ephrem_the_syrian_deacon.bio: A deacon of Nisibis and Edessa, called the 'Harp of the Spirit' for his hymns and poetry. A Doctor of the Church.

gregory_of_narek_abbot.bio: An Armenian monk and poet whose Book of Lamentations is a classic of Armenian literature. Named a Doctor of the Church in 2015.

immaculate_heart_of_mary.bio: The day after the feast of the Sacred Heart, the Church honors the heart of Mary, who 'kept all these things, pondering them in her heart.'

irenaeus_of_lyon_bishop.bio: A disciple of Polycarp, who had known St. John. As bishop of Lyon he wrote Against Heresies. Named a Doctor of the Church in 2022.

john_baptist_de_la_salle_priest.bio: A French priest who founded the Brothers of the Christian Schools and pioneered teacher training. He is patron of teachers.

juan_diego_cuauhtlatoatzin.bio: An Indigenous Mexican to whom the Virgin Mary appeared at Tepeyac in 1531, leaving her image on his cloak: Our Lady of Guadalupe.

lawrence_of_brindisi_priest.bio: A Capuchin friar, preacher and diplomat who knew many languages. He led troops into battle holding only a crucifix. A Doctor of the Church.

louis_ix_of_france.bio: King of France renowned for justice and care for the poor. He built the Sainte-Chapelle and died on crusade near Tunis.

margaret_mary_alacoque_virgin.bio: A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial whose visions of Christ spread devotion to his Sacred Heart throughout the Church.

margaret_of_scotland.bio: An English princess who became Queen of Scotland. She reformed the Church there, founded abbeys and served the poor at her own table.

mary_mother_of_the_church.bio: The Monday after Pentecost honors Mary, who prayed with the apostles in the upper room as the Church was born, as Mother of the whole Church.

most_sacred_heart_of_jesus.bio: The heart of Christ, pierced on the cross, as the sign of his love for all people. 'Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened.'

nicholas_of_myra_bishop.bio: Bishop of Myra, famed for secret gifts to the poor—the origin of Santa Claus. He is patron of children, sailors and Russia.

our_lady_of_guadalupe.bio: In 1531 the Virgin Mary appeared to St. Juan Diego at Tepeyac, near Mexico City, leaving her image on his cloak. She is patroness of the Americas.

our_lord_jesus_christ_king_of_the_univer.bio: The last Sunday of the Church's year proclaims Christ as King of all creation, whose kingdom is 'of truth and life, of holiness and grace, of justice, love and peace.'

pancras_of_rome_martyr.bio: A boy of fourteen martyred in Rome under Diocletian. Churches dedicated to him, including in London, spread his name widely.

peter_chrysologus_bishop.bio: Bishop of Ravenna, whose short, vivid sermons earned him the name 'Golden Word'. A Doctor of the Church.

raymond_of_penyafort_priest.bio: A Dominican canon lawyer who compiled the Church's decrees and served as Master of his order. Legend says he sailed from Majorca on his cloak.

rita_of_cascia_religious.bio: Wife, mother and widow who became an Augustinian nun at Cascia. She is invoked as patron of impossible causes.

stanislaus_of_szczepanow_bishop.bio: Bishop of Kraków, killed while celebrating Mass after rebuking King Bolesław II. He is a patron of Poland.

therese_of_the_child_jesus_and_the_holy_.bio: A Carmelite nun of Lisieux who died at twenty-four. Her 'little way' of trust and love, told in Story of a Soul, made her a Doctor of the Church.

andre_bessette_religious.bio: A frail, barely literate Holy Cross brother who served for decades as doorkeeper of a Montreal college. His prayers to St. Joseph drew thousands of the sick, and he built the great Oratory of St. Joseph on Mount Royal.

andrew_kim_tae_gon_priest_paul_chong_ha_.bio: Andrew Kim was the first Korean-born priest, beheaded at twenty-five. With the lay catechist Paul Chong and 101 companions, he is honored among the martyrs of the Church in Korea.

anthony_mary_claret_bishop.bio: A Catalan weaver turned priest and missionary, he founded the Claretians and served as archbishop of Santiago, Cuba, and confessor to the Queen of Spain.

anthony_zaccaria_priest.bio: A doctor from Cremona who became a priest and founded the Barnabites. He spread devotion to the Eucharist and to the letters of St. Paul, and died at thirty-six.

callistus_i_pope.bio: Once a slave, he became a deacon in charge of the Christian cemetery on the Appian Way that bears his name, then pope. He was martyred in Rome.

christopher_magallanes_priest_and_compan.bio: A Mexican parish priest shot during the Cristero persecution after absolving his executioners. He is honored with twenty-four companions, priests and lay people.

cornelius_i_pope_and_cyprian_of_carthage.bio: Pope Cornelius and Bishop Cyprian of Carthage stood together for mercy toward Christians who had lapsed under persecution. Both died for the faith.

damien_de_veuster_priest.bio: A Belgian priest who volunteered to serve the leper colony on Molokaʻi, Hawaii. He built homes, a church and a community there, and died of leprosy himself.

faustina_kowalska_virgin.bio: A Polish nun whose diary of visions spread devotion to the Divine Mercy and the image inscribed 'Jesus, I trust in you.'

frances_xavier_cabrini_virgin.bio: An Italian missionary who founded schools, orphanages and hospitals for immigrants in the Americas. The first U.S. citizen to be canonized, she is patron of immigrants.

francis_xavier_seelos_priest.bio: A Bavarian Redemptorist who served German immigrants across the United States. He died in New Orleans after caring for victims of yellow fever.

john_bosco_priest.bio: A Turin priest who gathered poor and abandoned boys, teaching them trades and faith with patience and good humor. He founded the Salesians and is patron of young people.

john_eudes_priest.bio: A French priest and preacher who founded seminaries and religious congregations, and promoted devotion to the Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

john_nepomucene_neumann_bishop.bio: A Bohemian immigrant who became bishop of Philadelphia. He built the first diocesan Catholic school system in the United States and was the first American bishop to be canonized.

john_paul_ii_pope.bio: Karol Wojtyła of Kraków, pope from 1978 to 2005. He travelled the world, helped bring down communism in Eastern Europe, and called young people to 'Be not afraid.'

john_xxiii_pope.bio: Angelo Roncalli, the warm-hearted 'Good Pope John', who opened the Second Vatican Council in 1962 to renew the Church.

josephine_bakhita_virgin.bio: Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold into slavery, she was freed in Italy, became a Canossian sister and was loved for her gentleness. She is patron of Sudan and of victims of trafficking.

junipero_serra_priest.bio: A Franciscan from Majorca who founded the first nine missions of California. He was canonized in 2015.

justin_martyr.bio: A philosopher who found in Christianity 'the only sure and useful philosophy'. His writings defended the faith to the emperor, and he was beheaded in Rome.

kateri_tekakwitha_virgin.bio: A Mohawk-Algonquin woman baptized at twenty, who lived a life of prayer and penance near Montreal. The 'Lily of the Mohawks' is the first Native American saint.

katharine_drexel_virgin.bio: A Philadelphia heiress who gave her fortune and life to found schools for Native American and Black students, including Xavier University of Louisiana.

lawrence_ruiz_and_companions_martyrs.bio: A Filipino husband and father who joined Dominican missionaries to Japan and was martyred at Nagasaki with fifteen companions. He is the first Filipino saint.

louis_grignion_de_montfort_priest.bio: A French missionary preacher whose True Devotion to Mary taught total consecration to Jesus through Mary.

marcellinus_of_rome_and_peter_the_exorci.bio: A priest and an exorcist of Rome, martyred under Diocletian. Their names are recalled in the Roman Canon of the Mass.

maria_goretti_virgin.bio: An Italian farm girl of eleven who died resisting an attacker and forgave him before she died. He repented and was present at her canonization.

marianne_cope_virgin.bio: A Franciscan sister from Syracuse, New York, who led nuns to care for leprosy patients in Hawaiʻi and continued Father Damien's work on Molokaʻi.

marie_rose_durocher_virgin.bio: A Canadian who founded the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus and Mary to educate children in Quebec.

martin_de_porres_religious.bio: The son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed Black woman in Lima, he became a Dominican brother known for his care of the sick and the poor. He is patron of social justice.

maximilian_mary_raymund_kolbe_priest.bio: A Polish Franciscan who founded the Knights of the Immaculata. At Auschwitz he offered his life in place of a stranger with a family, and died in the starvation bunker.

miguel_agustin_pro_priest.bio: A Mexican Jesuit who ministered in secret during the persecution of the Church. Executed by firing squad, he died with arms outstretched, crying 'Viva Cristo Rey!'

our_lady_of_fatima.bio: In 1917 the Virgin Mary appeared six times to three shepherd children at Fátima, Portugal, calling for prayer of the Rosary and conversion.

paul_of_the_cross_priest.bio: An Italian mystic and preacher who founded the Passionists, devoted to preaching the Passion of Christ.

paul_vi_pope.bio: Giovanni Battista Montini, pope from 1963 to 1978, who brought the Second Vatican Council to completion and was the first pope to travel by plane to five continents.

peter_chanel_priest.bio: A French Marist missionary to Futuna in the Pacific, killed there; the whole island soon became Christian. He is the first martyr of Oceania.

peter_claver_priest.bio: A Spanish Jesuit in Cartagena, Colombia, who met every slave ship for forty years, nursing and baptizing the enslaved. He called himself 'the slave of the slaves forever.'

peter_damian_bishop.bio: A monk and cardinal who called the clergy to reform and wrote vividly on prayer. A Doctor of the Church.

peter_julian_eymard_priest.bio: A French priest devoted to the Eucharist who founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament.

pius_francesco_forgione_priest.bio: Padre Pio, a Capuchin friar of San Giovanni Rotondo who bore the stigmata for fifty years. Crowds came to his confessional and his Mass.

pius_x_pope.bio: Giuseppe Sarto, pope from 1903 to 1914, whose motto was 'to restore all things in Christ'. He encouraged frequent Communion and let children receive it young.

rose_philippine_duchesne_virgin.bio: A French Religious of the Sacred Heart who brought her order to Missouri, opening schools on the frontier. The Potawatomi called her 'Woman Who Prays Always.'

sharbel_makhluf_priest.bio: A Lebanese Maronite monk and hermit who lived in silence and prayer for twenty-three years. Countless healings have been attributed to his intercession.

teresa_benedicta_of_the_cross_stein_virg.bio: Edith Stein, a Jewish-born philosopher who became a Catholic and a Carmelite nun. She was murdered at Auschwitz and is a patron of Europe.

charles_lwanga_and_companions_martyrs.bio: Charles Lwanga, head of the royal pages of Buganda, protected the young pages in his care and was burned alive at Namugongo with Catholic and Anglican companions.

anthony_of_egypt_abbot.bio: An Egyptian who gave away his inheritance and went into the desert to pray, battling temptation for decades. Disciples gathered around him, and he is called the father of monks.

augustine_of_canterbury_bishop.bio: A Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great to the English. He baptized King Ethelbert of Kent and became the first Archbishop of Canterbury.

adalbert_of_prague_bishop.bio: A Czech nobleman who became Bishop of Prague, he left his troubled see to preach the Gospel to the pagan Prussians on the Baltic coast. He was killed there, and is a patron of Bohemia and Poland.

agatha_of_sicily_virgin.bio: A young Christian of Sicily who refused the advances of a Roman official and was tortured and imprisoned for her faith. She died in prison at Catania and is invoked against fire and breast disease.

agnes_of_rome_virgin.bio: A girl of about twelve who refused marriage, saying she was already promised to Christ, and was put to death in Rome. Her name is said in the Roman Canon of the Mass, and she is often shown with a lamb.

all_saints.bio: A feast for every saint in heaven, known and unknown: the 'great multitude which no one could count, from every nation.' It celebrates the holiness of ordinary men and women as much as the famous.

ambrose_of_milan_bishop.bio: A Roman governor who was acclaimed Bishop of Milan by the people before he was even baptized. A great preacher and hymn-writer, he stood up to emperors and baptized St. Augustine.

andrew_apostle.bio: A fisherman of Galilee and brother of Peter, he was the first apostle Jesus called. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross in Greece; he is patron of Scotland.

angela_merici_virgin.bio: An Italian laywoman who saw that girls needed education in the faith. In Brescia she founded the Ursulines, the first order of women devoted to teaching.

annunciation_of_the_lord.bio: The angel Gabriel announces to Mary that she will bear the Son of God, and she answers, 'Let it be done to me according to your word.' Nine months before Christmas, the Word becomes flesh.

anselm_of_canterbury_bishop.bio: An Italian-born monk of Normandy who became Archbishop of Canterbury and was twice exiled for defending the Church against kings. His motto, 'faith seeking understanding', made him a father of scholastic theology.

ansgar_of_hamburg_bishop.bio: A Benedictine monk who carried the Gospel to Denmark and Sweden and became the first Archbishop of Hamburg. He is called the Apostle of the North.

anthony_of_padua_priest.bio: A Portuguese priest who joined St. Francis's friars and became the most celebrated preacher of his age. Legend says even the fish rose to listen; he is invoked to find lost things.

assumption_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.bio: At the end of her earthly life, Mary was taken body and soul into the glory of heaven. One of the oldest Marian feasts, it is kept on August 15 throughout the Church.

augustine_zhao_rong_priest_and_companion.bio: Augustine Zhao Rong, a soldier who became a priest, died in prison in 1815. He is honored with 119 others, Chinese and missionary, martyred over three centuries and canonized together in 2000.

barnabas_apostle.bio: A Cypriot Jew whose name means 'son of encouragement', he vouched for the newly converted Paul and travelled with him on the first missionary journey. Tradition says he was martyred on Cyprus.

basil_the_great_and_gregory_nazianzen_bi.bio: Two friends from Cappadocia who studied together in Athens and became bishops and great defenders of the faith in the Trinity. Basil also wrote a rule for monks; Gregory was called 'the Theologian'.

bede_the_venerable_priest.bio: A monk of Jarrow in northern England who spent his life studying, teaching and writing. His Ecclesiastical History of the English People earned him the title 'Father of English History'.

benedict_of_nursia_abbot.bio: A young Roman who left the city to pray as a hermit, then founded monasteries, including Monte Cassino. His Rule of 'pray and work' shaped Western monastic life; he is patron of Europe.

bernard_of_clairvaux_abbot.bio: A French Cistercian abbot whose eloquence moved popes and kings and helped spread his order across Europe. His writings on the love of God and devotion to Mary earned him the name 'the honey-sweet doctor'.

bonaventure_of_bagnoregio_bishop.bio: An Italian Franciscan who taught in Paris alongside Thomas Aquinas and led his order for seventeen years. A cardinal and Doctor of the Church, he wrote the Journey of the Mind to God.

bruno_of_cologne_priest.bio: A German scholar who left a brilliant career at Reims to seek God in silence. In the mountains near Grenoble he founded the Carthusians, monks who live as hermits in community.

catherine_of_alexandria_virgin.bio: According to legend, a learned young noblewoman of Alexandria who out-argued the emperor's philosophers and converted them. Sentenced to be broken on a spiked wheel, which shattered, she was beheaded.

chair_of_saint_peter_the_apostle.bio: A feast of the authority Christ gave Peter to teach and lead his Church: 'You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.' The chair is a symbol of the pope's office.

charles_borromeo_bishop.bio: A nephew of Pope Pius IV, made a cardinal at twenty-two, he became the model reforming bishop of Milan after the Council of Trent. During the plague of 1576 he stayed to feed and nurse the sick.

clare_of_assisi_virgin.bio: A noblewoman of Assisi who ran away at eighteen to follow St. Francis in poverty. She founded the Poor Clares and led them from San Damiano for forty years.

clement_i_pope.bio: The fourth Bishop of Rome, who may have known Peter and Paul. His letter to the quarreling church at Corinth is one of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament.

conversion_of_saint_paul_the_apostle.bio: On the road to Damascus to arrest Christians, Saul is thrown to the ground by a light from heaven and hears, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?' The persecutor becomes the Apostle to the Gentiles.

cosmas_of_cilicia_and_damian_of_cilicia_.bio: Twin brothers, physicians in Syria, who were known as 'the unmercenaries' because they treated the sick for free. They were martyred under Diocletian and are patrons of doctors.

cyril_constantine_the_philosopher_monk_a.bio: Two Greek brothers from Thessaloniki sent to evangelize the Slavs. They invented an alphabet to translate the Scriptures and liturgy into Slavonic, and are patrons of Europe.

cyril_of_jerusalem_bishop.bio: Bishop of Jerusalem, exiled three times in the controversies of his age. His lectures to those preparing for baptism give a vivid picture of the early Church's faith and worship.

dedication_of_the_basilica_of_saint_mary.bio: The great Roman church of Mary, rebuilt after the Council of Ephesus proclaimed her Mother of God in 431. Legend says its site was marked by a miraculous snowfall in August.

dedication_of_the_basilicas_of_saints_pe.bio: A feast of the two great Roman basilicas raised over the tombs of the apostles: St. Peter's on the Vatican Hill and St. Paul's Outside the Walls.

dedication_of_the_lateran_basilica.bio: The Lateran is the cathedral of the Bishop of Rome, dedicated in 324, and called 'the mother and head of all churches of the city and the world.'

denis_of_paris_bishop_and_companions_mar.bio: The first Bishop of Paris, beheaded on the hill now called Montmartre, 'the martyrs' mount', with the priest Rusticus and the deacon Eleutherius. Legend says he walked away carrying his head.

dominic_de_guzman_priest.bio: A Spanish priest who saw that the heresies of southern France could be met only by poor, learned preachers. He founded the Order of Preachers, the Dominicans, and is linked with the Rosary.

epiphany_of_the_lord.bio: Wise men from the East follow a star to Bethlehem and kneel before the child with gold, frankincense and myrrh. Christ is revealed to all the nations.

exaltation_of_the_holy_cross.bio: A feast of the cross on which Christ died, recalling the finding of the True Cross in Jerusalem and the dedication of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in 335. The instrument of death becomes the sign of victory.

first_martyrs_of_the_holy_roman_church.bio: After the great fire of Rome, Nero blamed the Christians. Many were crucified, thrown to beasts or burned as living torches in his gardens—the first martyrs of the Church of Rome.

frances_of_rome_religious.bio: A Roman noblewoman, wife and mother, who spent her wealth on the poor during plague and famine. She founded a community of women to serve them, and it was said her guardian angel was visible to her.

francis_of_assisi.bio: The son of a rich merchant who gave up everything to live in poverty and joy, preaching peace and caring for lepers. He founded the Franciscans, received the stigmata, and is patron of animals and the environment.

francis_of_paola_hermit.bio: A Calabrian hermit whose followers became the Minims, 'the least of all', vowed to a life of fasting and humility. King Louis XI called him to France, where he died.

francis_xavier_priest.bio: One of St. Ignatius's first companions, he sailed for Asia and preached the Gospel in India, Malaysia and Japan. He died on an island off the coast of China and is patron of missions.

gregory_vii_pope.bio: Hildebrand, a monk who became pope in 1073, fought to free the Church from control by kings and to reform the clergy. He famously made the emperor Henry IV wait in the snow at Canossa.

hedwig_of_silesia_religious.bio: A Bavarian-born duchess of Silesia who used her position to found hospitals and monasteries. After her husband's death she lived among the nuns of Trzebnica, serving the poor.

hilary_of_poitiers_bishop.bio: A married pagan philosopher who became a Christian and Bishop of Poitiers. Exiled for defending the divinity of Christ, he wrote a great work on the Trinity and was teacher to St. Martin.

holy_family_of_jesus_mary_and_joseph.bio: A feast of the home at Nazareth, where Jesus grew 'in wisdom and age and grace' with Mary and Joseph. It is kept in the octave of Christmas as a model for every family.

holy_innocents_martyrs.bio: The little boys of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ. They are honored as the first to die for him.

independence_day.bio: The anniversary of the Declaration of Independence of 1776. The Church in the United States gives thanks for the nation and prays for liberty and justice for all.

jerome_emiliani.bio: A Venetian soldier who was captured in war and freed, he believed, by Mary's help. He gave his life to orphans and the homeless and is patron of orphans and abandoned children.

jerome_of_stridon_priest.bio: A brilliant and fiery scholar who lived as a monk in Bethlehem and translated the Bible into Latin. His Vulgate was the Church's Bible for over a thousand years; he is patron of translators.

joachim_and_anne_parents_of_mary.bio: According to ancient tradition, the parents of the Virgin Mary and grandparents of Jesus. They are honored together as patrons of grandparents.

john_i_pope.bio: A Tuscan who became pope and was sent by the Arian Ostrogoth king Theodoric on a mission to Constantinople. On his return the king threw him into prison at Ravenna, where he died.

john_of_capistrano_priest.bio: An Italian lawyer and governor who became a Franciscan and a tireless preacher across Europe. At seventy he helped lead the defense of Belgrade against the Ottoman army.

john_of_god_duarte_cidade_religious.bio: A Portuguese shepherd, soldier and bookseller who, after a dramatic conversion, opened a hospital in Granada for the poor and sick. His followers became the Brothers Hospitallers.

joseph_spouse_of_mary.bio: A carpenter of Nazareth, a just and silent man, who took Mary as his wife and raised Jesus as his own son. He is patron of the universal Church, of fathers and of a happy death.

joseph_the_worker.bio: A feast of St. Joseph the carpenter, set on May Day in 1955 to honor the dignity of human work. Jesus himself was known as 'the carpenter's son.'

lawrence_of_rome_deacon.bio: A deacon of Rome in charge of the Church's goods. Ordered to hand over its treasures, he brought the poor and said, 'Here are the treasures of the Church.' He was martyred on a gridiron.

lucy_of_syracuse_virgin.bio: A young Christian of Sicily who gave her dowry to the poor and was martyred under Diocletian. Her name means 'light', and her feast falls in the darkest days of the year.

luke_evangelist.bio: A Greek physician and companion of St. Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles. Tradition says he painted the first icon of the Virgin; he is patron of doctors and artists.

mark_evangelist.bio: John Mark, a companion of Paul, Barnabas and Peter, wrote the earliest of the Gospels. Tradition makes him the founder of the Church of Alexandria; his relics rest in Venice.

martha_of_bethany_mary_of_bethany_and_la.bio: Friends of Jesus who welcomed him into their home at Bethany: busy Martha, Mary who sat at his feet, and Lazarus, whom Jesus wept for and raised from the dead.

martin_i_pope.bio: A pope who held a council condemning an imperial heresy, he was arrested by the emperor's soldiers, tried in Constantinople and exiled to the Crimea, where he died of hunger and cold.

martin_of_tours_bishop.bio: A Roman soldier who cut his cloak in half to give to a freezing beggar, and that night saw Christ wearing it. He became a monk and Bishop of Tours, one of the most beloved saints of Europe.

mary_magdalene.bio: A follower of Jesus from Galilee, freed by him from seven demons, who stood by the cross and was first to see him risen. She is called 'the apostle to the apostles.'

matthew_apostle.bio: A tax collector at Capernaum who left his booth when Jesus said, 'Follow me.' Tradition names him as the author of the first Gospel, and as a martyr.

michael_gabriel_and_raphael_archangels.bio: The three archangels named in Scripture: Michael, who casts down Satan; Gabriel, who brought the news to Mary; and Raphael, who guided Tobias and healed his father.

most_holy_body_and_blood_of_christ.bio: Corpus Christi, a feast of the Eucharist, in which Christ gives his body and blood under the forms of bread and wine. It is traditionally marked by processions through the streets.

most_holy_name_of_jesus.bio: The name given to the child at his circumcision, meaning 'God saves.' 'At the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven and on earth.'

most_holy_name_of_mary.bio: A feast of the name of the Mother of God, spread throughout the Church after the relief of Vienna from the Ottoman siege in 1683.

most_holy_trinity.bio: A feast of the central mystery of the faith: one God in three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. It is kept on the Sunday after Pentecost.

nativity_of_john_the_baptist.bio: The birth of John to the aged Elizabeth and Zechariah, who regained his voice to name him. One of the few saints whose birthday is celebrated, six months before Christmas.

nativity_of_the_lord.bio: Christmas: the Son of God is born of the Virgin Mary in a stable at Bethlehem and laid in a manger, while angels sing to shepherds in the fields.

norbert_of_xanten_bishop.bio: A worldly German courtier converted after a near miss by lightning. He founded the Premonstratensians at Prémontré and became Archbishop of Magdeburg, a champion of the Eucharist.

passion_of_saint_john_the_baptist.bio: John was imprisoned for telling King Herod his marriage was unlawful. At a birthday feast, Herodias's daughter danced and asked for his head on a platter.

patrick_of_ireland_bishop.bio: Kidnapped from Britain as a boy and enslaved in Ireland, he escaped, became a priest, and returned to convert the Irish. Legend says he used the shamrock to explain the Trinity.

paul_miki_and_companions_martyrs.bio: A Japanese Jesuit, son of a samurai, who was crucified at Nagasaki with twenty-five companions—priests, brothers, laymen and boys. From the cross he forgave his executioners.

pentecost_sunday.bio: Fifty days after Easter, the Holy Spirit descends on the apostles and Mary as tongues of fire, and they go out to preach in every language. It is the birthday of the Church.

peter_and_paul_apostles.bio: The fisherman whom Christ made the rock of his Church, and the persecutor who became the Apostle to the Gentiles. Both were martyred in Rome—Peter crucified upside down, Paul beheaded.

philip_and_james_apostles.bio: Philip of Bethsaida, who brought Nathanael to Jesus and asked, 'Show us the Father,' and James, son of Alphaeus, often identified with the leader of the Church in Jerusalem.

polycarp_of_smyrna_bishop.bio: Bishop of Smyrna and a disciple of St. John the Apostle. Told to curse Christ, he answered, 'Eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong,' and was burned alive.

pontian_i_pope_and_hippolytus_of_rome_pr.bio: A pope and a rival scholar-priest who had broken with him, both sent to the mines of Sardinia. There they were reconciled and died as martyrs.

presentation_of_the_blessed_virgin_mary.bio: According to an ancient tradition, Mary as a little girl was brought by her parents to the Temple in Jerusalem and dedicated to God.

presentation_of_the_lord.bio: Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple, where old Simeon takes him in his arms and calls him 'a light for revelation to the Gentiles.' Candles are blessed today.

scholastica_of_nursia_virgin.bio: Twin sister of St. Benedict and founder of a convent near Monte Cassino. At their last meeting her prayer brought a storm that kept him talking with her through the night.

simon_and_jude_apostles.bio: Simon the Zealot and Jude Thaddeus, apostles who, tradition says, preached together in Persia and were martyred there. Jude is invoked as patron of hopeless causes.

stephen_i_of_hungary.bio: The first King of Hungary, crowned with a crown sent by the pope in 1000. He brought the faith to his people, founded dioceses and is revered as the father of the nation.

stephen_the_first_martyr.bio: One of the first seven deacons, 'full of grace and power.' Stoned to death in Jerusalem, he prayed for his killers as a young man named Saul looked on.

sylvester_i_pope.bio: Pope during the reign of Constantine, when the Church emerged from persecution. In his time the first great basilicas of Rome were built and the Council of Nicaea was held.

teresa_of_calcutta_virgin.bio: An Albanian nun who left her teaching convent to serve 'the poorest of the poor' in the slums of Calcutta. Her Missionaries of Charity now care for the dying and abandoned worldwide.

teresa_of_jesus_of_avila_virgin.bio: A Spanish Carmelite nun, mystic and reformer who founded seventeen convents and wrote The Interior Castle. Bold and humorous, she was the first woman named a Doctor of the Church.

thanksgiving_day.bio: A national day of gratitude to God for the harvest and the blessings of the year, kept on the fourth Thursday of November.

thomas_apostle.bio: The apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection until he touched the wounds, then cried, 'My Lord and my God!' Tradition says he carried the Gospel to India.

transfiguration_of_the_lord.bio: On a high mountain Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John, his face shining like the sun, as Moses and Elijah appear beside him and a voice says, 'This is my beloved Son.'

vincent_de_paul_priest.bio: A French peasant's son who became a priest and gave his life to the poor, the sick and galley slaves. With St. Louise de Marillac he founded the Daughters of Charity.

vincent_ferrer_priest.bio: A Spanish Dominican and one of the great preachers of the Middle Ages, who travelled across Europe calling crowds to repentance and worked to heal the Great Schism.

vincent_of_saragossa_deacon.bio: A deacon of Saragossa in Spain, tortured to death at Valencia under Diocletian. He is the first martyr of Spain and patron of winemakers.

visitation_of_mary.bio: Mary hurries to visit her cousin Elizabeth, and the child in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy. Mary answers with her great hymn of praise, the Magnificat.

ash_wednesday.bio: The first day of Lent. Ashes are marked on the forehead with the words, 'Remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return.'

thursday_of_the_lords_supper.bio: Holy Thursday: at the Last Supper Jesus washes his disciples' feet, gives them his body and blood, and says, 'Do this in memory of me.'

advent_1_sunday_a.bio: “Watch therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.”

advent_1_sunday_b.bio: “What I say to you I say to all: Watch.”

advent_1_sunday_c.bio: “Now when these things begin to take place, look up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”

advent_2_sunday_a.bio: “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

advent_2_sunday_b.bio: “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.”

advent_2_sunday_c.bio: “All flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

advent_3_sunday_a.bio: “The blind receive their sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.”

advent_3_sunday_b.bio: “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord.’”

advent_3_sunday_c.bio: “I baptize you with water; but he who is mightier than I is coming, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.”

advent_4_sunday_a.bio: “Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel, which means, God with us.”

advent_4_sunday_b.bio: “Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.”

advent_4_sunday_c.bio: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!”

lent_1_sunday_a.bio: “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.’”

lent_1_sunday_b.bio: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent, and believe in the gospel.”

lent_1_sunday_c.bio: “It is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.’”

lent_2_sunday_a.bio: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him.”

lent_2_sunday_b.bio: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”

lent_2_sunday_c.bio: “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”

lent_3_sunday_a.bio: “But whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst; the water that I shall give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life.”

lent_3_sunday_b.bio: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

lent_3_sunday_c.bio: “Let it alone, sir, this year also, till I dig about it and put on manure. And if it bears fruit next year, well and good; but if not, you can cut it down.”

lent_4_sunday_a.bio: “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know; one thing I know, that though I was blind, now I see.”

lent_4_sunday_b.bio: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.”

lent_4_sunday_c.bio: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was yet at a distance, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him.”

lent_5_sunday_a.bio: “I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live.”

lent_5_sunday_b.bio: “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”

lent_5_sunday_c.bio: “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to throw a stone at her.”

easter_time_3_sunday_a.bio: “Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us on the road, while he opened to us the scriptures?”

easter_time_3_sunday_b.bio: “See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; handle me, and see; for a spirit has not flesh and bones as you see that I have.”

easter_time_3_sunday_c.bio: “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.”

easter_time_4_sunday_a.bio: “The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy; I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly.”

easter_time_4_sunday_b.bio: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”

easter_time_4_sunday_c.bio: “My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me; and I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand.”

easter_time_5_sunday_a.bio: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father, but by me.”

easter_time_5_sunday_b.bio: “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in me, and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.”

easter_time_5_sunday_c.bio: “A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; even as I have loved you, that you also love one another.”

easter_time_6_sunday_a.bio: “I will not leave you desolate; I will come to you.”

easter_time_6_sunday_b.bio: “Greater love has no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.”

easter_time_6_sunday_c.bio: “If a man loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him.”

easter_time_7_sunday_a.bio: “This is eternal life, that they know you the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.”

easter_time_7_sunday_b.bio: “Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.”

easter_time_7_sunday_c.bio: “That they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.”

ordinary_time_2_sunday_a.bio: “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!”

ordinary_time_3_sunday_a.bio: “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.”

ordinary_time_4_sunday_a.bio: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”

ordinary_time_5_sunday_a.bio: “You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hid.”

ordinary_time_6_sunday_a.bio: “Think not that I have come to abolish the law and the prophets; I have come not to abolish them but to fulfil them.”

ordinary_time_7_sunday_a.bio: “But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”

ordinary_time_8_sunday_a.bio: “But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be yours as well.”

ordinary_time_9_sunday_a.bio: “Every one then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house upon the rock.”

ordinary_time_10_sunday_a.bio: “Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.’ For I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.”

ordinary_time_11_sunday_a.bio: “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; pray therefore the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.”

ordinary_time_12_sunday_a.bio: “Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? And not one of them will fall to the ground without your Father’s will. But even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not, therefore; you are of more value than many sparrows.”

ordinary_time_13_sunday_a.bio: “He who finds his life will lose it, and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.”

ordinary_time_14_sunday_a.bio: “Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

ordinary_time_15_sunday_a.bio: “As for what was sown on good soil, this is he who hears the word and understands it; he indeed bears fruit, and yields, in one case a hundredfold, in another sixty, and in another thirty.”

ordinary_time_16_sunday_a.bio: “Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.”

ordinary_time_17_sunday_a.bio: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls, who, on finding one pearl of great value, went and sold all that he had and bought it.”

ordinary_time_18_sunday_a.bio: “They need not go away; you give them something to eat.”

ordinary_time_19_sunday_a.bio: “Take heart, it is I; have no fear.”

ordinary_time_20_sunday_a.bio: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”

ordinary_time_21_sunday_a.bio: “I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the powers of death shall not prevail against it.”

ordinary_time_22_sunday_a.bio: “If any man would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.”

ordinary_time_23_sunday_a.bio: “For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I in the midst of them.”

ordinary_time_24_sunday_a.bio: “I do not say to you seven times, but seventy times seven.”

ordinary_time_25_sunday_a.bio: “So the last will be first, and the first last.”

ordinary_time_26_sunday_a.bio: “Truly, I say to you, the tax collectors and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.”

ordinary_time_27_sunday_a.bio: “Have you never read in the scriptures: ‘The very stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

ordinary_time_28_sunday_a.bio: “For many are called, but few are chosen.”

ordinary_time_29_sunday_a.bio: “Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”

ordinary_time_30_sunday_a.bio: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

easter_time_6_thursday.bio: “Truly, truly, I say to you, you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.”

easter_time_6_friday.bio: “So you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.”

easter_time_6_saturday.bio: “Hitherto you have asked nothing in my name; ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.”

easter_time_7_tuesday.bio: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son that the Son may glorify you.”
